sm: Ben Shapiro and his colleagues scroll through the Daily Wire website on Black Friday, treating it as a guided tour. They start with the film lineup, noting titles like Confession, Hacksaw Ridge, Run Hide Fight, Infidels and Bonhoeffer, and say the World War II era movies make a solid weekend. Some of the films are licensed rather than produced in house.

They move on to the Matt Walsh page, joking about a famous office photo of him waving people off with his hand. They look at his show, his documentaries Am I Racist and What Is a Woman, and his Real History collection, which one of them calls good for Thanksgiving.

Next they sample comedy and Michael Knowles. A clip of a feminist comedy set is quickly abandoned, and a Knowles episode about why he will not play Grand Theft Auto 6 draws jokes about getting paid to sit on a couch. A fashion clip has Knowles describing his merino wool collection knit in New York.

Finally they look at Matt Fradd's biblical content, including a video arguing the Lord of the Rings plot is not original and was influenced by Arthurian legend and Merlin. They mention that Advent content is coming and praise Morning Wire, the news show that covers the day's stories in fifteen minutes or less.

The group pulls up Isabel Brown, praising her thumbnails and her appeal to conservative women and moms. In a short clip she criticizes a New Yorker article asking when pregnancy really begins, calling it blatant propaganda and saying a person either is or is not pregnant.

They then browse the large Jordan Peterson library, covering marriage, parenting, depression, anxiety, vision and negotiation. In one clip Peterson says someone can have a high IQ and poor moral character, and that there is no correlation between morality and intelligence.

Finally Shapiro checks subscriber reactions to his James Bond rankings. Commenters agree Casino Royale is the best Bond film, one says Roger Moore was the best, and another says Brosnan, Dalton and Craig fell off. Someone also urges everyone to watch Mobland.
sg: Isabel Brown, Peterson, and Bond Rankings
